Which of the following is equivalent to the integral ∫CF⋅dr, where C is the closed polygonal path ABCA, shown in the diagram above, traversed in the clockwise direction?

a
−∫C1F⋅dr+∫C2F⋅dr+∫C3F⋅dr

∫C1F⋅dr−∫C2F⋅dr+∫C3F⋅dr
c
∫C1F⋅dr−∫C2F⋅dr−∫C3F⋅dr

decision.explanation: The clockwise path is A→B→C→A. The diagram orients C₁ from B→A, C₂ from B→C, and C₃ from A→C. Reversing a path negates its line integral, so the required sum is −∫C₁ F·dr + ∫C₂ F·dr − ∫C₃ F·dr.

Which of the following is equivalent to the integral ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r,$ where $C$ is the closed polygonal path $ABCA,$ shown in the diagram above, traversed in the **clockwise** direction?
after.worked_solution:
First, notice that we can represent $C,$ which is traversed clockwise, as the union of $3$ paths:

$$
C={-{C}_{1}}\cup {C}_{2}\cup {-{C}_{3}},
$$

where $-{C}_{1}$ and $-{C}_{3}$ are the same paths as ${C}_{1}$ and ${C}_{3}$ but traversed in the opposite direction.

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{-{C}_{1}}F\cdot \text{d}r+{\int }_{{C}_{2}}F\cdot \text{d}r+{\int }_{-{C}_{3}}F\cdot \text{d}r \\  & =-{\int }_{{C}_{1}}F\cdot \text{d}r+{\int }_{{C}_{2}}F\cdot \text{d}r-{\int }_{{C}_{3}}F\cdot \text{d}r.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 1
?

Which of the following is equivalent to the integral ∫CF⋅dr, where C is the closed polygonal path ABCA, shown in the diagram above, traversed in the clockwise direction?

a
−∫C1F⋅dr+∫C2F⋅dr+∫C3F⋅dr
b
∫C1F⋅dr−∫C2F⋅dr+∫C3F⋅dr
c
∫C1F⋅dr−∫C2F⋅dr−∫C3F⋅dr
d
−∫C1F⋅dr+∫C2F⋅dr−∫C3F⋅dr
e
∫C1F⋅dr+∫C2F⋅dr+∫C3F⋅dr
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

First, notice that we can represent C, which is traversed clockwise, as the union of 3 paths:

C={−C1}∪C2∪{−C3},

where −C1 and −C3 are the same paths as C1 and C3 but traversed in the opposite direction.

Therefore, we obtain

∫CF⋅dr=∫−C1F⋅dr+∫C2F⋅dr+∫−C3F⋅dr=−∫C1F⋅dr+∫C2F⋅dr−∫C3F⋅dr.

verification.explanation: The worked solution confirms option d. Clockwise traversal A→B→C→A reverses C₁ and C₃ while following C₂, giving negative signs for C₁ and C₃ and a positive sign for C₂.

Which of the following is equivalent to the integral ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r,$ where $C$ is the closed polygonal path $ABCA,$ shown in the diagram above, traversed in the **clockwise** direction?
content.worked_solution:
First, notice that we can represent $C,$ which is traversed clockwise, as the union of $3$ paths:

$$
C={-{C}_{1}}\cup {C}_{2}\cup {-{C}_{3}},
$$

where $-{C}_{1}$ and $-{C}_{3}$ are the same paths as ${C}_{1}$ and ${C}_{3}$ but traversed in the opposite direction.

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{-{C}_{1}}F\cdot \text{d}r+{\int }_{{C}_{2}}F\cdot \text{d}r+{\int }_{-{C}_{3}}F\cdot \text{d}r \\  & =-{\int }_{{C}_{1}}F\cdot \text{d}r+{\int }_{{C}_{2}}F\cdot \text{d}r-{\int }_{{C}_{3}}F\cdot \text{d}r.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 2

Which of the following is equivalent to the integral ∫CF⋅dr, where C is the closed polygonal path TUVT, shown in the diagram above, traversed in the clockwise direction?

a
−∫C1F⋅dr+∫C2F⋅dr−∫C3F⋅dr
b
−∫C1F⋅dr−∫C2F⋅dr+∫C3F⋅dr
c
∫C1F⋅dr+∫C2F⋅dr−∫C3F⋅dr
d
−∫C1F⋅dr+∫C2F⋅dr+∫C3F⋅dr
e
∫C1F⋅dr−∫C2F⋅dr−∫C3F⋅dr
Submit

decision.explanation: Clockwise traversal T→U→V→T reverses C₁ (U→T) and follows C₂ (U→V) and C₃ (V→T). Reversing a path negates its line integral, giving −∫C₁ F·dr + ∫C₂ F·dr + ∫C₃ F·dr.

Which of the following is equivalent to the integral ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r,$ where $C$ is the closed polygonal path $TUVT,$ shown in the diagram above, traversed in the **clockwise** direction?
after.worked_solution:
First, notice that we can represent $C,$ which is traversed in clockwise, as the union of $3$ paths:

$$
C={-{C}_{1}}\cup {C}_{2}\cup {C}_{3},
$$

where $-{C}_{1}$ is the same path as ${C}_{1}$ but traversed in the opposite direction.

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{-{C}_{1}}F\cdot \text{d}r+{\int }_{{C}_{2}}F\cdot \text{d}r+{\int }_{{C}_{3}}F\cdot \text{d}r \\  & =-{\int }_{{C}_{1}}F\cdot \text{d}r+{\int }_{{C}_{2}}F\cdot \text{d}r+{\int }_{{C}_{3}}F\cdot \text{d}r.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 2
?

Which of the following is equivalent to the integral ∫CF⋅dr, where C is the closed polygonal path TUVT, shown in the diagram above, traversed in the clockwise direction?

a
−∫C1F⋅dr+∫C2F⋅dr−∫C3F⋅dr
b
−∫C1F⋅dr−∫C2F⋅dr+∫C3F⋅dr
c
∫C1F⋅dr+∫C2F⋅dr−∫C3F⋅dr
d
−∫C1F⋅dr+∫C2F⋅dr+∫C3F⋅dr
e
∫C1F⋅dr−∫C2F⋅dr−∫C3F⋅dr
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, notice that we can represent C, which is traversed in clockwise, as the union of 3 paths:

C={−C1}∪C2∪C3,

where −C1 is the same path as C1 but traversed in the opposite direction.

Therefore, we obtain

∫CF⋅dr=∫−C1F⋅dr+∫C2F⋅dr+∫C3F⋅dr=−∫C1F⋅dr+∫C2F⋅dr+∫C3F⋅dr.

$$
C={-{C}_{1}}\cup {C}_{2}\cup {C}_{3},

$$

$$

$$
{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r={\int }_{{C}_{1}}F\cdot \text{d}r+{\int }_{{C}_{2}}F\cdot \text{d}r.

The path ${C}_{1}$ is the horizontal line segment from $O$ to $A.$ It can be parametrized as

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{1}(t) & =0+t(a-0) \\  & =⟨0,0⟩+t(⟨1,0⟩-⟨0,0⟩) \\  & =⟨t,0⟩ \\  & =t\,i,\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}F({r}_{1}(t))\cdot {r}_{1}^{′}(t) & =({t}^{2}\,i+t\,j)\cdot (i) \\  & ={t}^{2}\end{aligned}

$$

Question 5
?

Let F(x,y,z)=2zi+3xj−4yk and let C be a path in R3. Which of the following is equivalent to ∫CF⋅dr?

a
∫C2zdx+3xdy−4ydz
b
∫C−4ydx+2zdy+3xdz
c
∫C(2z+3x−4y)dxdydz
d
∫C3xdx−4ydy+2zdz
e
∫C2dx+3dy−4dz
Submit

decision.explanation: Since dr=i dx+j dy+k dz, the dot product is F·dr=2z dx+3x dy−4y dz. Integrating along C gives option a.

after.name: Question 5
after.problem: Let $F(x,y,z)=2z\,i+3x\,j-4y\,k$ and let $C$ be a path in ${R}^{3}.$ Which of the following is equivalent to ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r?$
after.worked_solution:
Given a piecewise-smooth path $C$ and a vector field 

$$
F(x,y,z)=P(x,y,z)\,i+Q(x,y,z)\,j+R(x,y,z)\,k
$$

defined on $C,$ we have

$$
{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r={\int }_{C}P(x,y,z)\,\text{d}x+Q(x,y,z)\,\text{d}y+R(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z.
$$

Therefore, in our case, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{C}2z\,\text{d}x+3x\,\text{d}y-4y\,\text{d}z.\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

Given a piecewise-smooth path C and a vector field F(x,y,z)=P(x,y,z)i+Q(x,y,z)j+R(x,y,z)k defined on C, we have

∫CF⋅dr=∫CP(x,y,z)dx+Q(x,y,z)dy+R(x,y,z)dz.

Therefore, in our case, we obtain ∫CF⋅dr=∫C2zdx+3xdy−4ydz.

content.problem: Let $F(x,y,z)=2z\,i+3x\,j-4y\,k$ and let $C$ be a path in ${R}^{3}.$ Which of the following is equivalent to ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r?$
content.worked_solution:
Given a piecewise-smooth path $C$ and a vector field 

$$
F(x,y,z)=P(x,y,z)\,i+Q(x,y,z)\,j+R(x,y,z)\,k
$$

defined on $C,$ we have

$$
{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r={\int }_{C}P(x,y,z)\,\text{d}x+Q(x,y,z)\,\text{d}y+R(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z.
$$

Therefore, in our case, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{C}2z\,\text{d}x+3x\,\text{d}y-4y\,\text{d}z.\end{aligned}
$$
